title: Usage of ChatGPT on English Language Skills of Students at Maputi Senior High School
venue: Psychology and Education: A Multidisciplinary Journal
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether Grade 12 students’ use of ChatGPT is associated with better English language skills, focusing specifically on grammar and vocabulary. The authors note growing educational interest in ChatGPT but argue that empirical evidence on its relationship to specific language sub-skills remains limited, especially in secondary education. Their research questions address how often students use ChatGPT, why they use it, how efficient they perceive it to be, whether those usage dimensions relate to grammar and vocabulary performance, and whether ChatGPT users differ from non-users.

The study did not test a controlled intervention. Instead, it used a quantitative correlational design comparing naturally occurring groups of ChatGPT users and non-users. Data were collected through a self-administered questionnaire with Likert-scale items on frequency, purpose, and efficiency of ChatGPT use, plus a 20-item multiple-choice assessment of grammar and vocabulary. Analyses included descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations, and independent-samples t-tests.

Participants were 117 Grade 12 students at a single secondary school, Maputi Senior High School in Misamis Oriental, Philippines. The sample was drawn by simple random sampling from a Grade 12 population of 365 students and included 72 ChatGPT users and 45 non-users. The study setting was the school context, but the paper does not describe a classroom-based implementation, teacher-led use, or any structured instructional treatment involving ChatGPT.

The main conclusion is that ChatGPT use, as measured in this sample, was infrequent and was not significantly associated with grammar or vocabulary performance. Students generally did not report using ChatGPT primarily for grammar or vocabulary improvement and rated it as only slightly efficient for language learning purposes. Independent-samples t-tests also found no significant differences between users and non-users on grammar or vocabulary scores. The authors conclude that access to or use of ChatGPT alone does not necessarily improve these English language skills and recommend more guided, pedagogically sound integration and future experimental research.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed quantitative correlational study with a defined sample and reported reliability, but it is non-experimental, uses self-reported ChatGPT exposure, and does not identify a controlled writing-feedback intervention or causal assignment.
impact_tier_rationale: Findings consistently indicate no statistically significant benefit of ChatGPT use on grammar or vocabulary, and computed standardized differences between users and non-users are trivial.

interventions.use_case: General student use of ChatGPT as a conversational AI tool for English-language support among Grade 12 students, including self-reported use for grammar improvement, vocabulary expansion, creative writing, reading comprehension, and communication practice.
ChatGPT used specifically as an English language aid for grammar, vocabulary, and writing development rather than as a full curricular tutor.

finding.finding_summary: Among Grade 12 students at Maputi Senior High School (total n=117; 72 ChatGPT users, 45 non-users), ChatGPT use was not associated with better English literacy-related subskills. Independent-samples t-tests found no significant user/non-user differences in vocabulary (users M=7.44, SD=2.10; non-users M=7.09, SD=2.19; t(115)=0.875, p=0.383) or grammar (users M=8.42, SD=3.49; non-users M=8.24, SD=3.08; t(115)=0.271, p=0.787); overall scores were described as 'failed to meet expectations.'
finding.measure: Researcher-administered 20-item multiple-choice English language skills assessment covering grammar and vocabulary; user vs non-user group comparisons and correlations with ChatGPT usage indices
finding.effect_size: approximately d=0.16 for vocabulary; approximately d=0.05 for grammar (computed from reported means/SDs)
finding.std_deviation: Vocabulary: users SD=2.10, non-users SD=2.19; Grammar: users SD=3.49, non-users SD=3.08

finding.finding_summary: The study operationalized English language skill as grammar and vocabulary performance and found no significant relationships between ChatGPT usage dimensions and these language outcomes. Correlations between frequency/purpose of use and grammar or vocabulary were small and non-significant (reported r values around 0.093-0.100, p>0.40), and efficiency correlations were also non-significant (grammar r=0.131, p=0.273; vocabulary r=0.092, p=0.442) among the ChatGPT-user subsample.
finding.measure: Pearson correlations between self-reported ChatGPT frequency, purpose, and efficiency and grammar/vocabulary scores
finding.study_size: n=72 for correlation analyses (df=70 implies ChatGPT-user subsample)
